problem:
If $g(x)$ is left-continuous at $x=5$ and $g(5)=5,$ then

${lim}_{x\to {5}^{-}}\frac{g(x)-{x}^{2}}{4x}=$
 {{field-1}}.
worked_solution:
Since $g(x)$ is left-continuous at $x=5,$ we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to {5}^{-}}g(x)=g(5)=5.
$$

Consequently,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {5}^{-}}\frac{g(x)-{x}^{2}}{4x} & =\frac{{lim}_{x\to {5}^{-}}g(x)-\text{ }{lim}_{x\to {5}^{-}}{x}^{2}}{{lim}_{x\to {5}^{-}}4x} \\  & =\frac{5-{5}^{2}}{4(5)} \\  & =\frac{5-25}{20} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
